prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1487; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured's driver, who is named on the policy. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The officer's description of the scene lines up with the account given to us.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two witnesses and the other driver. Each describes the accident in the same way, and none of them contradicts the others on the sequence of events.

Entry 4: Photographs of the vehicles were reviewed. The damage is mostly consistent with the impact described, with the front-end crush and airbag deployment matching a head-on contact at low speed.

Entry 5: Reviewed the claimant's first medical records, which report neck and back strain. The kind of injury reported fits the force of a collision of this type.

Entry 6: No prior injury or treatment to the neck or back has come up in records or in discussion with counsel so far.

Entry 7: Checked vehicle history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 8: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the claimant's account. The claimant has given the same description of the accident in every conversation so far.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this kind. Requested updated treatment notes and billing to understand the course of care.

Entry 10: Received the updated records. The treating provider's notes are consistent with the earlier reports, and the extended treatment is documented with reasons for each visit.

Entry 11: Claim remains open pending review of the final bills and the attorney's demand. Next step is to schedule a file review once those documents arrive.
